summary: The window closes with a sharp escalation in US–China economic conflict: on the final day the U.S. Treasury Department issued a formal designation against China (item text truncated, but it is an official Treasury designation of the country itself), coinciding with a city-wide general strike in Hong Kong that halted transport, cancelled over 200 flights and was accompanied by a sharp drop in the Hang Seng Index. A third, smaller escalation on the same day was the UK joining a US-led naval mission in the Persian Gulf after Iranian seizures of oil tankers. The clustering of a state-level economic action against the world's second-largest economy with visible financial-market disruption in Hong Kong on the flagged day is the most plausible account of a regime change in volatility.
mechanism: A formal U.S. Treasury designation against China raises the perceived risk of a broader currency and trade confrontation, repricing exchange rates, export-exposed equities and safe-haven assets; simultaneously the Hong Kong general strike produced an observable equity drawdown and transport shutdown in a major Asian financial centre, and Gulf naval escalation adds an oil-supply risk premium.

claims.claim: On the final day of the window the U.S. Treasury Department issued a formal designation concerning China (the specific term is missing from the item text).
On the same day, a Hong Kong city-wide general strike with sit-ins in seven districts cancelled over 200 flights, halted MTR lines, and coincided with a sharp fall in the Hang Seng Index.
Hong Kong unrest had been building through the window, with mass protests near China's Liaison Office in defiance of a police ban and violence against pro-democracy activists.
The Hong Kong Chief Executive publicly rejected protester demands and blamed them for 'destroying Hong Kong'.
Also on the final day, the United Kingdom joined a US-led naval mission in the Persian Gulf to protect oil tankers after seizures by Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps.
US–Iran tensions had escalated earlier in the window when the U.S. Treasury sanctioned Iran's Foreign Minister.
Separate geopolitical frictions during the window included North Korean missile tests into the Sea of Japan and a US threat to consider a blockade of Venezuela.

competing_explanation: The Hong Kong general strike alone could account for the flagged change, since it is the only item that explicitly reports a market move (a sharp Hang Seng drop) and it caps two weeks of escalating unrest; on that reading the Treasury designation is incidental. A weaker alternative is that Gulf escalation — Iranian tanker seizures, sanctions on Iran's foreign minister and the UK joining the US naval mission — drove an oil-linked volatility increase.
